q-75203.name: Question 1
q-75203.problem: Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨t,\,{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ at the point where $t=0,$  valid for all  real values of $u?$
q-75203.worked_solution:
At the point where $t=0$,  the vector ${r}^{′}(0)$ is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at $P$ can be parametrized as

 

$$
R(u)=r(0)+u{r}^{′}(0),\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

 

First, we find $r(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨0,\,{e}^{0},\,{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

   

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{-t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${r}^{′}(t)$ at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0) & =⟨1,\,{e}^{0},\,-{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point 
 where $t=0$ is

$$
R(u)=⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩+u⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩,\,u\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 1
?

Which of the following gives the equation of the tangent to the curve r(t)=⟨t,et,e−t⟩ at the point where t=0, valid for all real values of u?

a
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨1,1,−1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
b
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨1,0,1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
c
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨−1,−1,−1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
d
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨1,−1,0⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
e
⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨0,−1,1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

At the point where t=0, the vector r′(0) is tangent to the curve, so the tangent line to the curve at P can be parametrized as

R(u)=r(0)+ur′(0),u∈(−∞,∞)

First, we find r(0):

r(0)=⟨0,e0,e−0⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩

Now, we calculate r′(t):

r′(t)=⟨ddt(t),ddt(et),ddt(e−t)⟩=⟨1,et,−e−t⟩

Then, we evaluate r′(t) at t=0:

r′(0)=⟨1,e0,−e−0⟩=⟨1,1,−1⟩

Finally, the tangent line to the given curve at the point where t=0 is
R(u)=⟨0,1,1⟩+u⟨1,1,−1⟩,u∈(−∞,∞).

q-126900.name: Question 2
q-126900.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}-2t,4t-1⟩,$ find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨-1,1⟩.$
q-126900.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-2,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨-1\,,\,1⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c⟨-1,1⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c⟨-1,1⟩ \\ ⟨2t-2,4⟩ & =c⟨-1,1⟩ \\ ⟨2t-2,4⟩ & =⟨-c,c⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2t-2=-c \\ 4=c\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we obtain that $c=4.$ Substituting $c=4$ into the first equation, we get $t=-1.$ 

Therefore, $⟨-1,1⟩$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the point corresponding to $t=-1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(-1) & =⟨(-1)^{2}-2(-1),4(-1)-1⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-5⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨-1,1⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(3,-5).$

q-126902.name: Question 3
q-126902.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2{t}^{2}-t,5-3{t}^{2}⟩,$ find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨-1,2⟩.$
q-126902.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨4t-1,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨-1\,,\,2⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c⟨-1,2⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c⟨-1,2⟩ \\ ⟨4t-1,-6t⟩ & =c⟨-1,2⟩ \\ ⟨4t-1,-6t⟩ & =⟨-c,2c⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}4t-1=-c \\ -6t=2c\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain that $c=-4t+1.$ Substituting $c=-4t+1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-6t & =2(-4t+1) \\ -6t & =-8t+2 \\ 2t & =2 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $⟨-1,2⟩$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the point corresponding to $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨2(1)^{2}-1,5-3(1)^{2}⟩=⟨1,2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨-1,2⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(1,2).$

q-164833.name: Question 4
q-164833.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2{t}^{5}\,,\,{t}^{2}-2⟩,$ $t\in (0,\infty ),$ find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector $⟨1\,,\,-5⟩.$
q-164833.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{5})\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨10{t}^{4}\,,\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors  $⟨1\,,\,-5⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $⟨1\,,\,-5⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨1\,,\,-5⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ⟨1\,,\,-5⟩\cdot ⟨10{t}^{4}\,,\,2t⟩ & =0 \\ 1\cdot 10{t}^{4}+(-5)\cdot 2t & =0 \\ 10{t}^{4}-10t & =0 \\ 10t({t}^{3}-1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (0,\infty )$, the only solution is $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨2(1)^{5}\,,\,(1)^{2}-2⟩=⟨2\,,\,-1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

q-165038.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{5}-8,2{t}^{4}-6⟩,$ $t\in (0,\infty )$, find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩.$
q-165038.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{5}-8),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-6)⟩ \\  & =⟨5{t}^{4},8{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\ ⟨5{t}^{4},8{t}^{3}⟩ & =c⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\ ⟨5{t}^{4},8{t}^{3}⟩ & =⟨c,\frac{4c}{5}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{t}^{4}=c \\ 8{t}^{3}=\frac{4c}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we obtain that $c=5{t}^{4}.$ Substituting $c=5{t}^{4}$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{t}^{3} & =\frac{4(5{t}^{4})}{5} \\ 8{t}^{3}-4{t}^{4} & =0 \\ 4{t}^{3}(2-t) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (0,\infty )$, the only solution is $t=2.$ 

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2) & =⟨(2)^{5}-8,2(2)^{4}-6⟩=⟨24,26⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨1,\frac{4}{5}⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(24,26).$
